findings.title: Acquired-company staff liked competitor app's streak/gamification feature
findings.description: Roland mentions that employees from the smaller acquired company (which used a competitor product) liked a streak/gamification feature in that app. He explicitly states his own people don't care about streaks and he isn't worried about it. This is competitive/comparison chatter, not a request to change BetterBark's product, and the customer does not ask for anything to be built.
findings.quote: the app had some kind of streak feature, gamification stuff. My people don't care about streaks, so I'm not worried
findings.severity_reason: No product defect and no request; purely informational competitive remark with explicitly stated lack of concern.
findings.match_note: Competitive/gamification chatter, not a BetterBark product gap the customer is asking to close; no catalogue analog.

findings.title: Hybrid vs. remote training-hours culture clash from acquisition integration
findings.description: Roland notes the acquired fully-remote company's staff are used to scheduling training on their own time, whereas Quarry Heights is hybrid, so there will be a 'small negotiation' internally about training-during-work-hours norms. Derek confirms the product already flexes to either remote or hybrid work models and that the change needed is internal messaging on Roland's side, not anything on BetterBark's end. Roland agrees this is just something he wanted to flag, not urgent, likely a Q4 conversation.
findings.quote: that acquired company was fully remote, and we're hybrid. So the training-during-work-hours norm is going to be a small negotiation.
findings.severity_reason: Explicitly resolved as a customer-side internal messaging/culture issue; product already supports both work models per staff confirmation.
findings.match_note: Not a product defect or missing capability — product already handles both scenarios; issue is customer's internal change management.

findings.title: Newly acquired staff (no prior pet benefit) asking about BetterBark access
findings.description: Roland reports that employees from one of the two newly acquired companies, which previously had no pet benefit at all, have heard about BetterBark and are asking about it. Derek frames this as future seat-expansion/sales conversation and explicitly declines to turn the check-in into a sales call. This is demand/expansion chatter, not a product defect or feature gap.
findings.quote: One of the two companies had no pet benefit at all and their people have already heard about ours and are asking.
findings.severity_reason: Purely a commercial/seat-expansion topic with no product defect or feature request involved.
findings.match_note: Sales/expansion interest, not a product capability gap; not actionable as a product ticket.
